mainTopic: Making up the קרבן חגיגה on the later days of the רגל and on שמיני עצרת, and what 'make-up' (תשלומין) means
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. The rule against bringing the חגיגה on the later days applies only when the first day had not yet ended; if the day ran out, he may go back and offer. A new משנה then teaches that someone who missed the חגיגה on the first day of סוכות may bring it all through the רגל, even on שמיני עצרת. Once the רגל passes, he owes nothing. The משנה applies the פסוק 'what is crooked cannot be made straight,' and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי each give their own reading of that פסוק. The גמרא finds the source for שמיני עצרת in a גזירה שוה on the word 'עצרת,' and shows the word is extra. It also brings a ברייתא that reads the same rule from 'אותו' and 'seven days.' Next, רבי יוחנן and רבי אושעיא disagree about what 'make-up' means, and רבי זירא shows that the dispute matters for a חיגר who was healed on the second day. The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from his ruling about a נזיר, and רבי ירמיה answers that טומאה is different because of פסח שני. רב פפא then begins an objection that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Limiting the rule: only when he did not finish
steps.stepSummary: An earlier teaching said the חגיגה is brought on the first day and not on all seven days. That teaching is now limited to a case where he 'did not finish.' If he 'finished,' he may go back and bring more.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only taught this rule where he did not finish. But if he finished, he may go back and offer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows an earlier rule: the rule that he may not keep bringing חגיגה offerings on the later days applies only when he 'did not finish.' The word 'finish' is left unclear on purpose, and the next step will ask what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule sounded absolute: the first day is when you bring the חגיגה, not every day of the חג. This statement creates an exception. In some situation called 'finished,' he is allowed to keep offering on the later days. This matters for the wider debate in which רבי יוחנן holds that the later days are only a make-up for the first day.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this rule in a case where… (a formula that limits an earlier rule)
Finished, completed
He goes back and offers (brings more קרבנות)

phrases.english: They only taught this where he did not finish,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the earlier teaching: bring the חגיגה on the first day, not on all seven days.

phrases.english: but if he finished, he goes back and offers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits an earlier teaching (from before this section) about bringing the חגיגה on the first day rather than on all seven days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule against continuing to offer on later days applies only when he 'did not finish'; if he 'finished,' he may go back and offer.

steps.title: What does 'finished' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'finished' means. It tests the obvious reading, 'finished his offerings,' and shows that reading makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'finished' mean? If you say he finished his offerings, then what is he going back to offer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'finished' means in the last step. It rejects the first idea that comes to mind. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'finished' meant he had already brought all his קרבנות, he would have nothing left to bring. So 'he goes back and offers' would be meaningless. 'Finished' must therefore refer to something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asks for the meaning of a word)
If you say… (introduces a possible reading that will be rejected)
His offerings

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'finished' means 'finished his offerings.' That is exactly the reading the גמרא rejects here.

phrases.english: What does 'finished' mean?
If you say he finished his offerings,
what is he offering?
phrases.notes: He means: if they're all done, there is nothing left to go back and bring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the key word in step 1 and rules out the obvious reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word 'גָּמַר' in the limiting statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all his offerings were done, there would be nothing left for him to go back and offer.

steps.title: 'Finished' means the day ended
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'finished' means the day finished. If the first day is still going and he stops with offerings left over, he cannot bring them later. If the day ended before he was done, he may go back and offer them on the later days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means where the day did not end. But if the day ended, he goes back and offers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning: 'finished' refers to the day ending, not to his offerings. The same words are repeated, now with this new meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose he stopped offering while the first day still had time, so he passed up a chance he had. Then he may not bring the leftover offerings on the other days. But if the day ran out before he could finish, he may continue bringing them later in the חג. This means even רבי יוחנן admits the חגיגה can sometimes be brought on the remaining days.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the correct explanation)
The day

steps.whatToRemember: 'Finished' means the day ended. If the first day ran out before he finished, he may bring the rest of his חגיגה offerings on the later days.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוחנן, who sees the later days as only a make-up for the first day, still allows offering on them in this case.

phrases.english: Rather, where the day did not end,
phrases.notes: The day still had time and he still had offerings left, so he may not save them for later days.

phrases.english: but if the day ended, he goes back and offers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by redefining 'finished' as the day ending.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'גָּמַר' means the day ended. If the day ended before he was done, he may continue offering on later days. If the day did not end and he stopped, he may not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even according to רבי יוחנן, someone whose first day ran out before he finished his חגיגה offerings may bring them on the remaining days of the חג.

steps.title: The משנה: missing the first day can be made up all through the חג
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if someone did not bring his חגיגה on the first יום טוב of סוכות, he can bring it on any day of the רגל, even the last יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who did not bring the חגיגה on the first יום טוב of the חג brings it during the whole רגל, and on the last יום טוב of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that the חגיגה missed on the first day of סוכות can be brought on any later day of the חג, including the final יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'חג' as a verb means bringing the קרבן חגיגה. The first day is the main time for it, but the remaining days and the last יום טוב (שמיני עצרת) also work. This gives the later days a make-up role.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Brought / brings the קרבן חגיגה
The pilgrimage festival
The last יום טוב of סוכות, meaning שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג —
phrases.english: One who did not bring the festival offering on the first יום טוב of the חג
brings it during the entire festival
and on the last יום טוב of the חג.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed חגיגה from the first day of סוכות may be brought on any day of the רגל, including שמיני עצרת.

steps.title: After the רגל passes, there is no make-up
steps.stepSummary: Once the whole רגל is over and he never brought his חגיגה, he has no obligation to replace it. The משנה applies the פסוק about what is crooked and cannot be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the רגל passed and he did not bring the חגיגה, he is not responsible for it. About this it says: 'What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is missing cannot be counted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues: once the חג is over, the missed חגיגה can no longer be made up. It supports this with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The make-up window lasts only as long as the רגל. After that, he owes nothing, even if he had set aside an animal and lost it. The פסוק describes a missed מצוה like this as a loss that can never be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Passed, went by
He is not responsible for it (does not have to replace it)
Something crooked
Something missing, a lack

steps.whatToRemember: The חגיגה can be made up during the whole רגל, including the last יום טוב. Once the רגל is over, the chance is gone for good.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Not responsible' here is not a leniency that lets him off lightly. It means the מצוה is lost and can no longer be made up.

phrases.english: If the festival passed and he did not bring the offering,
he is not responsible for it,
phrases.notes: Literally 'its responsibility.' He doesn't have to replace it, even if he had set aside an animal that was lost.

phrases.english: about this it is said:
'What is crooked cannot be made straight,'
'and what is missing cannot be counted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the outer limit of the make-up period given in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the רגל has passed without his bringing the חגיגה, he has no obligation to make it up; the מצוה is lost.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: crooked means fathering a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says the 'crooked that cannot be fixed' is a man who fathered a ממזר through a forbidden relationship. A thief cannot be the meaning, because a thief can return what he took.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: Who is the crooked one that cannot be fixed? It is someone who had relations with a forbidden woman and fathered a ממזר with her. If you say it means a thief or a robber, he can give it back and fix his sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a different way to read the same פסוק from Step 5. Here 'crooked' is a permanent sin, not a missed חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether the damage can ever be undone. A thief can return the object, so his sin can be fixed. A ממזר stays a ממזר forever, so that sin can never be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Crooked; something bent out of shape
To be fixed or made right
A woman forbidden to a man by the Torah
A child born from a forbidden relationship; this status is permanent
Someone who steals secretly or robs openly

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
Who is the crooked one that cannot be fixed?
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:15. This is the same פסוק the משנה used in Step 5.

phrases.english: This is one who had relations with a forbidden woman
and fathered a mamzer from her.
If you say it refers to one who steals or robs,
he can return it and fix his wrong.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְּיָיא אוֹמֵר: אֵיזֶהוּ מְעֻוָּות שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהִתָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the פסוק the משנה just used for a missed חגיגה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Crooked that cannot be fixed' means a man who fathered a ממזר, because that damage is permanent. A thief can still return what he took.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: crooked means a תלמיד חכם who left Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says 'crooked' only describes something that was once straight and became bent. That is a תלמיד חכם who leaves his Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: We only call something 'crooked' if it was straight at first and then became bent. Who is that? A תלמיד חכם who walks away from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A third reading of the same פסוק. This one focuses on what the word 'crooked' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי reads the word 'מעוות' closely. You can only call something bent if it was once straight. So the פסוק describes someone who had Torah and lost it, not someone who was never straight to begin with.

keyTerms.meaning: Straight, in good order, at the start
Became bent or crooked
A Torah scholar
Who separates himself from Torah learning

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three readings of 'what is crooked cannot be fixed': a missed חגיגה, fathering a ממזר, and a תלמיד חכם who left Torah.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
We do not call something 'crooked' except
one who was straight at first and then became crooked.
And who is this?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: This is a Torah scholar who leaves the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: אֵין קוֹרִין מְעֻוָּות אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different reading of the same פסוק, based on the meaning of the word 'crooked.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Crooked' only describes what was once straight, so the פסוק means a תלמיד חכם who abandoned Torah.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the חגיגה can be made up on the last day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the משנה's rule that the חגיגה can be brought even on the last יום טוב, שמיני עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens and asks for the source of the rule from Step 4. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמיני עצרת is its own holiday, separate from סוכות. So it is not obvious that a חגיגה missed on סוכות can be made up on it. The גמרא wants a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means the rule from Step 4: a missed חגיגה can be brought even on the last יום טוב, שמיני עצרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's main rule from Step 4 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that שמיני עצרת counts as a make-up day for the סוכות חגיגה.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from the word 'עצרת'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי ישמעאל, compares the seventh day of פסח and שמיני עצרת, since the Torah calls both 'עצרת.' The seventh day of פסח is a make-up day, so שמיני עצרת is one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: The word 'עצרת' is said about the seventh day of פסח, and 'עצרת' is said about the eighth day of סוכות. Just as there it is a day for making up, here too it is a day for making up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a גזירה שוה, a comparison based on the same word appearing in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the seventh day of פסח is part of פסח, so a missed חגיגה can be brought then. Since the Torah uses the same word 'עצרת' for שמיני עצרת, we learn that it works the same way. It is also a day for making up the חגיגה.

keyTerms.meaning: Assembly; a name the Torah gives to a closing holiday day
The seventh day of פסח
The eighth day of סוכות, שמיני עצרת
Making up an offering that was missed
Just as there, so too here; the wording of a גזירה שוה

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison runs in one direction. The seventh day of פסח is clearly a make-up day, and that fact is carried over to שמיני עצרת. It is not the other way around.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
'Assembly' is said about the seventh day of Pesach,
and 'Assembly' is said about the eighth day of the Festival.
Just as there it is for making up,
so too here it is for making up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: נֶאֱמַר עֲצֶרֶת בִּשְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on 'עצרת' links שמיני עצרת to the seventh day of פסח, so both are days for making up the חגיגה.

steps.title: The word is 'free,' so the comparison stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that 'עצרת' is an extra word, available for learning. Otherwise one could knock down the comparison: the seventh day of פסח is like the days before it, but שמיני עצרת is different from the days before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is free. For if it were not free, one could refute it: The seventh day of פסח is not different from the days before it. Can you say the same about the eighth day of סוכות, which is different from the days before it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks an attack on רבי יוחנן's גזירה שוה before anyone raises it. It says the word 'עצרת' is extra, so the comparison holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גזירה שוה can be broken by showing the two cases are different. Here they are different: the seventh day of פסח continues פסח, but שמיני עצרת is its own holiday. Since the word 'עצרת' is extra in the פסוקים (מופנה), the comparison stands even with that difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Free; the word is extra and set aside for learning a גזירה שוה
One could refute it, by pointing to a difference between the cases
Different from the days before it

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a גזירה שוה can stand even when the two cases are clearly different: the shared word must be extra.
steps.whatToRemember: שמיני עצרת is a make-up day for the סוכות חגיגה. This is learned from a גזירה שוה on 'עצרת' with the seventh day of פסח, and it holds because the word is מופנה.

phrases.english: It is free.
phrases.notes: The word 'עצרת' is extra in the פסוקים, so it is free to be used for this comparison.

phrases.english: For if it were not free, one could refute it:
What about the seventh day of Pesach?
It is not different from the days before it.
Can you say the same about the eighth day of the Festival,
which is different from the days before it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּפְנֶה. דְּאִי לָאו מוּפְנֶה, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the גזירה שוה of Step 9 against a possible refutation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seventh day of פסח is part of the same holiday, but שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday, so maybe they cannot be compared.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is מופנה (extra), so differences between the cases do not break the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without an extra word, the difference between the two days would break the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because 'עצרת' is מופנה, the גזירה שוה stands and שמיני עצרת is a make-up day.

steps.title: Proving the word 'עצרת' is truly extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that 'עצרת' is a free word. Its plain meaning, a ban on work, is already written elsewhere in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the word is surely free. After all, what does 'עצרת' mean? Held back from doing work. But the Torah already wrote 'you shall not do work.' So why did the Torah write 'עצרת'? Learn from this that it is free for learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the word 'עצרת' really is extra. That means the comparison from the last step cannot be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עצרת' means being held back from work. The very same פסוק already says 'you shall not do work,' so the word adds nothing to its plain meaning. An extra word like this is 'free,' and a free word can be used for a comparison that cannot be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Free, meaning an extra word with no other job, so it can be used for learning
Held back or stopped
Doing forbidden work
The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: Because the word is free, רבי יוחנן's source for bringing the חגיגה on שמיני עצרת stands firm.

phrases.english: No, it is certainly free.
After all, what does "עצרת" mean?
Held back from doing work.
But isn't it written: "You shall not do work"?
Why do I need the "עצרת" that the Merciful One wrote?
Rather, learn from it that it is free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the condition raised in step 10: the word really is extra, so the possible challenge falls away.
steps.raayaObject: That 'עצרת' is a free word, available for the comparison
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ban on work is already stated with 'לא תעשה מלאכה' in דברים 16:8, which makes 'עצרת' extra

steps.title: A ברייתא: the חגיגה belongs to the first day, and the seven days make up for it
steps.stepSummary: A תנא brings a different source. 'אותו' limits the חגיגה to the first day, and 'seven days' teaches that the rest of the days are make-up days.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא brings the rule from here, as a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall celebrate it as a festival to ה׳ seven days.' I might think a person may celebrate on any of the seven days as he likes. So the פסוק says 'it': it you celebrate, not all seven. If so, why say 'seven'? For make-up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source, from a ברייתא, for bringing the חגיגה on the later days. This step covers the seven days of סוכות, and the next step adds שמיני עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two words in the פסוק seem to pull in different directions. 'אותו' (it) points to one day, the first day. 'Seven days' points to the whole week. The ברייתא settles this: the first day is the main day, and the other days only serve as make-up days.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה, whose teachings appear in a ברייתא
And you shall celebrate, here meaning bringing the חגיגה offering
Keeps on celebrating, meaning he may bring the offering on any of the days
The פסוק teaches us to say
Make-up, a later chance to fulfill a missed obligation

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not all seven' does not mean the later days are useless. It means they are not equal to the first day. They are make-up days for it.

phrases.english: And a תנא brings it from here,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And you shall celebrate it as a festival to ה׳ seven days."

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהֵא חוֹגֵג וְהוֹלֵךְ כָּל שִׁבְעָה
phrases.english: I might think he may keep celebrating all seven days.
So the פסוק says: "it".
It you celebrate,
phrases.notes: "It" here means the first day of the festival.

phrases.english: and you do not celebrate all seven.
If so, why is "seven" said?
For make-up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing רבי יוחנן's source, the גמרא brings a different source from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חגיגה belongs to the first day of סוכות. The remaining days are make-up days.

steps.title: The ברייתא stretches the make-up to שמיני עצרת and no further
steps.stepSummary: 'In the seventh month' teaches that the make-up reaches even the last יום טוב, שמיני עצרת. 'אותו' stops it from going past the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that if a person did not celebrate on the first day of סוכות, he may celebrate the whole festival and the last יום טוב too? The פסוק says: 'In the seventh month you shall celebrate it.' If it only said 'in the seventh month,' I might think the whole month counts. So it says 'it': it you celebrate, and nothing outside of it.
steps.whatsHappening: This step finishes the ברייתא. It gives the תנא's source for the משנה's rule that the חגיגה may be brought even on שמיני עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In the seventh month' stretches the make-up time past the seven days of סוכות. 'אותו' then sets a limit, so the make-up does not run on for the whole month. Together, the two words reach exactly to the last יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A pilgrimage festival
The last יום טוב, meaning שמיני עצרת
Outside of it, beyond the festival days

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's source: 'אותו' makes the first day the main day, 'seven days' adds make-up days, 'in the seventh month' reaches שמיני עצרת, and the second 'אותו' stops there.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he did not celebrate
on the first יום טוב of the festival,
he may keep celebrating throughout the whole festival
and on the last יום טוב?
phrases.notes: This is שמיני עצרת, the day the משנה was talking about.

phrases.english: The פסוק says: "In the seventh month you shall celebrate it."
If it said only "in the seventh month,"

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהֵא חוֹגֵג וְהוֹלֵךְ הַחֹדֶשׁ כּוּלּוֹ
phrases.english: I might think he may keep celebrating the whole month.
So the פסוק says: "it".
It you celebrate,
and you do not celebrate outside of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם לֹא חָג יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, extending the make-up days to the last יום טוב.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that the חגיגה may be brought on שמיני עצרת

steps.title: What does 'make-up' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'תשלומין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'make-up' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'make-up' means in the ברייתא. This sets up the disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the seven days are 'for make-up,' but it did not say how they make up. The question is whether the later days only make up for the first day, or work in some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is it?

phrases.english: And what does "make-up" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the term 'תשלומין' used in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the make-up days relate to the first day and to each other

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי אושעיא disagree about 'make-up'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the later days make up for the first day. רבי אושעיא says the days make up for one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: make-up for the first day. רבי אושעיא said: make-up for one another.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the first day is the main day, and the rest of the days only make up for it. For רבי אושעיא, each day can count on its own, and the days make up for one another.

keyTerms.meaning: Make-up for the first day
Make-up for one another

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says the make-up days all depend on the first day. רבי אושעיא says the days make up for one another.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
Make-up for the first day.
And רבי אושעיא said:
Make-up for one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: the later days make up for the first day. רבי אושעיא: the days make up for one another.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a case where רבי יוחנן and רבי אושעיא would actually rule differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two explanations of תשלומין from the last step ever lead to a different ruling. This question sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two explanations can sound different but give the same result in every case. The גמרא wants a real case where the two views split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? A request for a practical case where two views disagree.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means רבי יוחנן and רבי אושעיא from the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the dispute stated in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case where the two definitions of תשלומין give different rulings.

steps.title: A person who was lame on the first day and healed on the second
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the views differ for someone who was a חיגר on day one and healed on day two. For רבי יוחנן he cannot bring; for רבי אושעיא he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The difference is a person who was lame on the first day and healed on the second day. רבי יוחנן says the later days make up for the first day. Since he was not fit on the first day, he is not fit on the second. רבי אושעיא says the days make up for one another. Even though he was not fit on the first day, he is fit on the second.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the case where the two views split: a person who could not bring on day one because he was lame, but was healed by day two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the later days only fix a first-day obligation that was missed. If there was no obligation on day one, there is nothing to make up. For רבי אושעיא, each day has its own obligation, so a person who becomes fit on day two must bring then.

keyTerms.meaning: A lame person, who is exempt from the מצוה of coming to the מקדש on the festival.
Was healed (literally, 'straightened out').
Make-up days for bringing the offering.
Fit or qualified.
Since; introduces the reason.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: no obligation on day one means no make-up later. רבי אושעיא: every day carries its own obligation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
One who was lame on the first day
phrases.notes: A lame person is exempt from coming up to the מקדש, so on day one he had no obligation.

phrases.english: and was healed on the second day
is the difference between them.
Rabbi Yochanan said: they are make-up for the first day,
so since he was not fit on the first day,
he is not fit on the second.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: תַּשְׁלוּמִין זֶה לָזֶה,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Oshaya said: they are make-up for one another,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא חֲזֵי בָּרִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: so even though he was not fit on the first day,
he is fit on the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: חִיגֵּר בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וְנִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּיוֹם שֵׁנִי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 with a concrete case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חיגר healed on day two: רבי יוחנן says he does not bring, and רבי אושעיא says he does.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן really hold this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן really says that someone unfit on day one has no obligation later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did רבי יוחנן really say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge to רבי יוחנן's view from step 17. It is setting up the next step, where it brings a ruling of his that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about רבי יוחנן's consistency. If he rules elsewhere that an obligation exists even when the offering cannot be brought, he should not say here that the חיגר is free.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say this? Introduces a contradiction from another statement of the same Sage.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's position as explained in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a person unfit on day one is not fit on day two.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ruling of רבי יוחנן seems to say that an obligation exists even when the offering cannot actually be brought.

steps.title: The case of becoming impure at night
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says that one who becomes impure in the day brings an offering, but not if it happens at night. רבי יוחנן says he brings even at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't חזקיה say: If he became impure in the daytime, he brings an offering; at night, he does not bring. And רבי יוחנן said: Even at night he also brings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind the challenge. It is a dispute where רבי יוחנן counts an obligation as real even at night, when offerings cannot be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה holds that since offerings cannot be brought at night, the new impurity does not create a new obligation. רבי יוחנן says it does, so for him being unable to bring does not cancel an obligation. That seems to clash with his ruling that a חיגר, who could not bring on day one, has no obligation to make up.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? Brings a source that contradicts.
Became ritually impure.
He brings an offering.
A person who took a vow of נזירות; the case discussed here.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this case is about the festival. It is a separate case about a נזיר, brought only to show how רבי יוחנן thinks about obligations that cannot be fulfilled at the moment.

phrases.english: But didn't Chizkiya say:
If he became impure in the day, he brings,
at night, he does not bring.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even at night he also brings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the evidence for the challenge raised in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds an obligation exists even when the offering cannot be brought at that moment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן about a נזיר who became impure at night.

steps.title: Impurity is different because it has a make-up
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that טומאה is a special case. The Torah gives an impure person a second chance, as with פסח שני, so being impure at the start does not cancel his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: טומאה is different, because it has a make-up, as we see with פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה defends רבי יוחנן against the contradiction from the last step. He explains that the impure person is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction was that in the נזיר case, רבי יוחנן counts the night as a time when the נזיר was fit to bring his offerings, even though offerings cannot be brought at night. That is why a second טומאה that night obligates him in a second set of offerings. רבי ירמיה says this proves nothing about a חיגר, because in the area of טומאה the Torah itself provides a make-up, as with פסח שני. So the general rule (unfit on day one means no make-up) still stands, and טומאה is the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different (it is a special case)
Ritual impurity
A make-up chance, a way to fill in what was missed
The second Pesach, a month later, for those who could not bring the קרבן פסח on time

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבי יוחנן consistent: being unfit at the start usually blocks a make-up, but טומאה is treated as an exception.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Impurity is different,
since it has a make-up
as we see with the second Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 18-19 by showing that טומאה is a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: טומאה differs from other kinds of unfitness because the Torah gives it a make-up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוחנן treats the night, when offerings cannot be brought, as a fit time for the נזיר, he should also hold that a person unfit on day one still had an obligation that can be made up later.
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאה is an exception because of the model of פסח שני. Other kinds of unfitness, like a חיגר, still have no make-up according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רב פפא begins to challenge the answer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא starts to object to רבי ירמיה. He says the answer works only according to one view about פסח שני. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected to it: This works well according to the one who says that פסח שני...
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins a challenge to רבי ירמיה's answer. This line is setting up the objection, which is finished in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה's proof rests on פסח שני being a make-up for the first פסח. רב פפא signals that not everyone may see פסח שני that way, so the proof would not work for everyone. The full objection is completed on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
This works well (setting up 'but according to the other view, it does not')
According to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: הָנִיחָא does not mean רב פפא agrees. It sets up a challenge: the answer works for one opinion, but not for the other.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to it:
This works well according to the one who says that the second Pesach

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's use of פסח שני as proof that טומאה has a make-up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's answer that טומאה is different because of פסח שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof from פסח שני only works if פסח שני is a make-up for the first פסח. If someone holds otherwise, the proof falls away. The objection is completed on the next amud.
